business_overview.title: Business Overview
business_overview.description: A document summarizing what this platform is, who it is for, and why it is needed now — from the operator's perspective.

vision.title: Vision
vision.content:
This platform is **not just POS software.**

It is a **food service operations platform** that connects a 4-tier business structure in a single system: store transactions → multi-location brand management → regional exclusive distribution → platform-wide governance.

Core value per tier:
- Store Owner: Protect revenue without theft/leakage, operate without language barriers
- Brand HQ: Control dozens of locations from one dashboard
- Distribution Partner: Earn stable revenue through exclusive regional distribution rights
- Platform Operator: Generate revenue from data and transaction flows across hundreds of brands, governing the entire ecosystem

product_tiers.title: 4-Tier Product Structure
product_tiers.content:
| Tier | Product | User | Core Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1: Store POS** | Edge POS | Owner, Manager, Cashier | Fast, accurate daily order/payment/inventory processing |
| **Tier 2: Brand Operations** | Brand Operations Portal | Brand HQ, Regional Manager | Manage menus/prices/staff/sales across all locations from one place |
| **Tier 3: Distribution** | Distribution Partner Portal | Distribution Partner | Recruit/sell/install/support stores via exclusive regional rights |
| **Tier 4: Platform Governance** | Platform Management System | Platform Operator | Contract/deploy/monitor all partners and brands; monetize data |

**Distribution Partner vs Platform Operator:**
- **Distribution Partner**: Signs an exclusive regional distribution contract with the Platform Operator. Directly recruits, sells, installs, and supports POS products/equipment to store owners in their territory. Responsible for local installation, training, and support.
- **Platform Operator**: The organization that plans, develops, and operates this entire project. Manages technology development, partner contracts, licensing policies, AI/data services, and global expansion strategy.

why_now.title: Why Now
why_now.content:
- Vietnam's food service market growing 15% annually — Korean restaurant brands expanding rapidly
- Existing POS systems are **single-store only** — incapable of multi-location/multi-country operations
- Top concern for Korean store owners: **Cannot trust local staff** → explosive demand for remote monitoring/control
- AI technology maturity — anomaly detection, demand forecasting, and auto-ordering are now production-ready
- Growing need for integrated order management across delivery apps (Fooding, GrabFood)

core_problem.title: Core Problem We Solve
core_problem.content:
**When the owner is not at the store, money leaks.**

- Employee discount abuse, cash shortfalls, inventory theft — 2~5% of revenue disappears
- Checking orders separately on each delivery app — missed orders, double-entry errors
- Korean-Vietnamese communication failures — order mistakes, customer complaints, staff turnover
- Headquarters cannot see location performance at a glance — problem stores are discovered too late
- Suppliers (distributors) manage each store individually — costs increase as they scale

This platform structurally solves these problems by connecting the information flow across all tiers: **Store → Brand → Distribution → Platform**.

participants.title: Participant Roles and Revenue
participants.content:
| Participant | Role | Revenue Source | Key Motivation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Platform Operator** | Technology development, overall ecosystem governance | Subscriptions + Data + Financial fees | Ecosystem expansion → revenue maximization |
| **Distribution Partner** | Exclusive regional distribution, store recruitment/sales/install/support | Subscription share + Procurement commissions | Exclusive territory → stable revenue |
| **Brand HQ** | Menu/pricing/policy management, multi-location ops | Revenue growth + Cost reduction | Multi-location efficiency |
| **Store Owner** | Daily transaction execution | Theft prevention + Cost savings | Operational stability |
| **Ingredient Suppliers** | Ingredient supply | Stable customer base | Bulk orders |
| **Financial Partners** | Micro-financing | Loan interest | Verified sales data |

**Key distinction**: The Platform Operator **builds** the product; the Distribution Partner **sells** it in their region. Partners sign exclusive distribution contracts and directly recruit, install, and support stores in their territory.

lockin.title: Lock-In Effect
lockin.content:
High switching costs at every tier make it difficult to switch to competitors:

- **Store Owner**: Transaction history data + Staff retraining + Delivery app re-integration
- **Brand**: Policy/menu rebuild + Report history loss + Reinstall at dozens of locations
- **Distribution Partner**: Exclusive contract + Local customer base + Installation/support infrastructure investment
- **Platform**: Data aggregate scale → Purchasing power → Supplier discounts → More signups (network effect)

pricing_strategy.title: Pricing Strategy
pricing_strategy.content:
**Korean Market (Premium):**
- KRW 150K~300K/mo/location (Theft Prevention + real-time translation justify premium)
- CCTV-integrated AI monitoring: +KRW 100K/mo
- Brand HQ analytics dashboard: +KRW 500K/mo

**Vietnamese Market (Penetration Pricing):**
- Basic POS features: Free or minimal fee
- Revenue recovered through food ingredient Group Purchasing commissions
- Premium features (AI analytics, inventory optimization): $30~100/mo

**Core Principle**: Secure cash through subscriptions in the Korean market → Expand the ecosystem through purchasing power in Vietnam

target_market.title: Target Market
target_market.description: A document outlining market size, customer segments, and regional market entry strategies.

segments.title: Customer Segments
segments.content:
### Priority 1: Korean Restaurant Owners in Vietnam

- **Size**: 3,000~5,000 Korean-owned restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City/Hanoi
- **Core Pain**: Trust issues with local staff, inability to manage remotely, language barrier
- **Willingness to Pay**: $150~300/mo (Theft Prevention + translation provide sufficient value)
- **Killer Feature**: CCTV-AI anomaly detection, bidirectional real-time translation
- **Go-to-Market**: Korean Chamber of Commerce, Korean restaurant communities, word of mouth

### Priority 2: Local Vietnamese Small-Medium Restaurants

- **Size**: 500K+ restaurants in Vietnam
- **Core Pain**: Monthly subscription burden, digital transformation challenges, ingredient cost pressure
- **Willingness to Pay**: $0~30/mo (instead pay via purchasing commissions)
- **Killer Feature**: Free POS + food ingredient Group Purchasing discounts
- **Go-to-Market**: Zalo communities, regional distributor networks

### Priority 3: Multi-Location Franchise Brands

- **Size**: 200+ franchises with 10+ locations in Vietnam
- **Core Pain**: HQ-location policy inconsistency, inability to compare performance, menu deployment delays
- **Willingness to Pay**: $500~3,000/mo/brand
- **Killer Feature**: Unified dashboard, one-click menu/price deployment
- **Go-to-Market**: B2B sales, pilot programs

entry_strategy.title: Market Entry Strategy
entry_strategy.content:
### Phase 1: Establish Beachhead (0~6 months)
- Target: 50 Korean-owned restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City
- Strategy: **Solve the trust problem** with CCTV-AI monitoring + real-time translation
- Goal: 60%+ paid conversion rate, $15K monthly revenue

### Phase 2: Local Expansion (6~18 months)
- Target: 500 local Vietnamese small-medium restaurants
- Strategy: **Free POS + food ingredient Group Purchasing** model
- Goal: $50K monthly revenue from purchasing commissions

### Phase 3: Franchise Acquisition (12~24 months)
- Target: 20 franchise brands with 10+ locations
- Strategy: Brand operations portal + AI analytics **premium package**
- Goal: $1K~3K/mo per brand, $40K monthly revenue

### Phase 4: Ecosystem Expansion (24+ months)
- Target: Expand into 2~3 additional Southeast Asian countries
- Strategy: Regional Distribution Partner contracts + white label
- Goal: Transition to platform transaction volume-based revenue model

competitive_landscape.content:
| Competitor | Strengths | Weaknesses | Our Differentiator |
|---|---|---|---|
| **KIS/KSNET** (Korea) | Card payment stability | Cannot expand overseas, no AI | Multi-country + AI + Translation |
| **Sapo POS** (Vietnam) | Local market share | Weak multi-location management, no Korean | Korea-Vietnam bidirectional |
| **Lightspeed** (Global) | Global brand | Weak localization, high pricing | Vietnam-specialized + Group Purchasing |
| **Grab POS** | Delivery integration | Basic POS features | Full-stack operations platform |

**Key Differentiator**: No competitor offers **CCTV-AI monitoring + real-time translation + food ingredient Group Purchasing** simultaneously.
